input_messages.content: Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m a bit worried. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else.
Okay, that sounds good. Please let me know what you need me to do next. I’m not very good with technical stuff, so I might need a bit of help.
On the top of my phone, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about service—just the airplane symbol. What does that mean?
Yes, please! I’m not sure how to turn off Airplane Mode. Can you walk me through it? I get nervous with these settings.
If you could do it for me, that would be wonderful—I always worry I’ll mess something up. Please go ahead and turn off Airplane Mode for me.
Okay, I think Airplane Mode is off now. But at the top of my phone, it says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled." I still don’t see any bars for signal. What should I do next?
I’m not sure how to do that myself—these menus always confuse me. Could you please guide me step by step, or if you can, turn on the mobile data for me? I just don’t want to press the wrong thing.

I tried to turn on mobile data, but it still says "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" at the top of my phone. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there something else I should try?
Alright, thank you for checking that. Please let me know what you find out or if there’s anything you need me to do next. I just want my phone to work again.

I’m not sure how to run any diagnostic commands myself—I wouldn’t even know where to start. If you could guide me step by step, that would be helpful. Or, if you can check it for me, that would be even better. What should I do?
I checked, and it looks like my phone is already set to "4G/5G preferred." Is there something else I should try? I still don’t have any signal showing.

I’m not sure how to run those commands—are they in the settings somewhere? I get confused with all these technical things. Could you please guide me step by step, or if you can check them for me, that would be much easier for me.

If you could guide me step by step, that would be helpful. I get overwhelmed with too many instructions at once, so maybe we can start with just one thing—maybe checking the SIM status? What should I look for?
I checked, and it says my SIM card is active and working. There aren’t any error messages or anything unusual showing. What should I do next?
I checked, and it looks like the APN name is set to "broken." I’m not sure what that means, but it doesn’t sound right. What should I do about this?

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said, but it says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. I get a bit nervous about restarting—will I lose my photos or anything important if I do this?
Okay, if you’re sure I won’t lose anything, I’ll go ahead and restart it. Could you please remind me how to do it, just to be safe? I always worry I’ll press the wrong button.
My phone is back on now, and I see signal bars at the top! It says "Excellent" and "5G." Thank you so much for your help—I was really worried, but it looks like it’s working again.
Thank you so much for your patience and help! I really appreciate it. I’ll let you know if I have any more trouble, but for now, I’m just relieved it’s working again. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

On the top of my phone, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about service—just the airplane symbol. What does that mean?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is currently turned ON on your phone. When Airplane Mode is ON, it disables all wireless communications, including cellular service, which is why you see "No Service."

To restore your cellular service, you need to turn OFF Airplane Mode on your phone. Would you like me to guide you on how to do that?

I will guide you through turning off Airplane Mode on your phone.

1. Look for the "Settings" app on your phone and open it.
2. In the Settings menu, find the option labeled "Network & Internet" or "Connections."
3. Inside that menu, you should see a toggle switch for "Airplane Mode."
4. If the toggle is ON (usually colored or to the right), tap it once to turn it OFF.
5. Once Airplane Mode is off, check the status bar again to see if the airplane icon disappears and if you start seeing signal bars.

If you want, I can also simulate turning off Airplane Mode for you now. Would you like me to do that?
If you could do it for me, that would be wonderful—I always worry I’ll mess something up. Please go ahead and turn off Airplane Mode for me.

2. Also, we will check if mobile data is turned off on your phone.
